learningObjectives.title: Types of galaxy and the Milky Way
The Big Bang and evidence for it

questions.q: Which type of galaxy is the Milky Way now classified as?
questions.explain: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy, with a central bar of stars from which the spiral arms extend.

questions.q: Approximately how many stars does the Milky Way contain?
questions.explain: The Milky Way is estimated to contain of the order of a few hundred billion stars.

questions.q: Which shape best describes an elliptical galaxy?
options: A rounded or oval ball of stars with no spiral arms
A flat disc with prominent spiral arms
A ring of gas with a hollow centre
A random, structureless cloud of stars
questions.explain: Elliptical galaxies are smooth, rounded or oval collections of stars lacking spiral arms.

questions.q: What is the approximate diameter of the Milky Way galaxy?
questions.explain: The disc of the Milky Way is roughly 100,000 light years across.

questions.q: Where is the Sun located within the Milky Way?
options: In a spiral arm, away from the galactic centre
Exactly at the centre of the galaxy
At the very edge of the galactic disc
questions.explain: The Sun lies within one of the spiral arms, tens of thousands of light years from the galactic centre, not at its core.

questions.q: What name is given to the nearest large spiral galaxy to the Milky Way?
questions.explain: The Andromeda Galaxy is the nearest large spiral galaxy to our own.

questions.q: Which type of galaxy has no regular or symmetrical shape?
questions.explain: Irregular galaxies lack the ordered structure of spiral or elliptical galaxies.

questions.q: In red-shift, the lines in a galaxy's spectrum are shifted towards which end of the spectrum?
questions.explain: Red-shift moves spectral lines towards the red, longer-wavelength end of the spectrum.

questions.q: What does the red-shift observed in the light from distant galaxies tell us?
options: The galaxies are moving away from us
The galaxies are moving towards us
questions.explain: Red-shift indicates the light source is receding, so distant galaxies are moving away from us.

questions.q: Which astronomer discovered the relationship between a galaxy's distance and its recession speed?
questions.explain: Edwin Hubble found that more distant galaxies recede faster, expressed by Hubble's law.

questions.q: According to Hubble's law, how does a galaxy's recession speed relate to its distance?
options: Speed is directly proportional to distance
Speed is inversely proportional to distance
Speed does not depend on distance
questions.explain: Hubble's law states v = H0 x d, so recession speed increases in direct proportion to distance.

questions.q: The light from the Andromeda Galaxy shows a blue-shift. What does this indicate?
options: Andromeda is moving towards the Milky Way
Andromeda is moving away from the Milky Way
questions.explain: Blue-shift means the spectral lines move to shorter wavelengths, showing the object is approaching.

questions.q: What key conclusion about the universe is drawn from the red-shift of distant galaxies?
options: The universe is unchanging in size
questions.explain: That almost all galaxies are receding, with speed rising with distance, shows the universe is expanding.

questions.q: Using v = H0 x d, a galaxy is 200 Mpc away and H0 = 70 km/s per Mpc. What is its recession speed?
Three galaxies lie at 50 Mpc, 150 Mpc and 400 Mpc. Which is receding fastest?
options: They all recede at the same speed
questions.explain: By Hubble's law recession speed rises with distance, so the most distant galaxy recedes fastest.

questions.q: According to the Big Bang theory, the universe began as a very hot, dense point and has been doing what ever since?
questions.explain: The Big Bang theory describes the universe expanding and cooling from an initial hot, dense state.

questions.q: Which pair of scientists first detected the cosmic microwave background radiation?
questions.explain: Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson detected the cosmic microwave background radiation in 1965.

questions.q: Why is the cosmic microwave background radiation (CMBR) regarded as strong evidence for the Big Bang?
options: It is the cooled-down remnant radiation left over from the early hot universe
It is light emitted by nearby stars today
It is caused by the Sun heating the Earth
It proves galaxies are moving towards us
questions.explain: The CMBR is leftover radiation from the hot early universe, now cooled to microwaves, as the Big Bang predicts.

questions.q: The CMBR is detected as radiation in which part of the electromagnetic spectrum?
questions.explain: The background radiation has cooled so that it now peaks in the microwave region of the spectrum.

questions.q: Which two observations together provide the main evidence supporting the Big Bang theory?
options: Red-shift of galaxies and the cosmic microwave background radiation
The phases of the Moon and solar flares
questions.explain: Galactic red-shift shows expansion and the CMBR is relic radiation, together forming the key evidence for the Big Bang.
